ai.description: Thackeray's Dwarf Gecko measures 46 mm. It is brown with a distinct yellow-orange vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Key features include a granular dorsal texture and a flattened tail base.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis thackerayi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow patch on its throat, which is absent in other sympatric dwarf gecko species.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis thackerayi* inhabits the granite rock outcrops of the southern Western Ghats, typically found in moist deciduous forests at elevations between 800 and 1,100 meters.
ai.behavior: Thackeray's dwarf gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects along the rocky crevices of its native Western Ghats habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis thackerayi* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis thackerayi* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu, India, specifically inhabiting rocky outcrops at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
